assessments.reasoning: Five contiguous parts cover the 78,949-byte SPDX json/details/CC-BY-3.0-AU.json, SHA-256 8b318b21ec347a9ab9f6be3a8d4aa52a62b7e190e6c0b2758b10fffbe2394edc. Part 1 gives isDeprecatedLicenseId=false and text headed “Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Australia”. Part 3 gives licenseId and both source fields.

The SPDX repository’s unsigned v3.29.0 tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b points to commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. That SHA is present in the raw URL for every part of the Australian 3.0 detail.

The publisher capture has the scoped digest 4d843eb65cbd3701b8d22c6d9b46726f439c636547aec60f5233af15ffc563e3 and the heading “Attribution 3.0 Australia”. Its canonical link is https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/au/legalcode.en. The receipt records the bare legalcode URL cited by SPDX.

challenge.method: Tested the 2.5 AU and 3.0 US alternatives against the ID, source URL and inline text. Compared the SPDX text and template with the publisher’s headings and section 5 list.
challenge.results: The 3.0 AU record has the Australian Capital Territory wording in section 13. Its plain text and the publisher use “Licence Grant”, while the template uses “License Grant”. Section 5 list numbering also differs between the plain text and the publisher HTML. Neither discrepancy changes the recorded identifier or citation.

limitations: The citation establishes correspondence for one capture and one SPDX release. Differences among the publisher HTML, SPDX text and template preclude treating them as a verbatim copy. Legal equivalence, translation, applicability to project files, grants, reuse, redistribution and installation are outside the finding.
